app_info.subtitle: Manage Zenthcloud resources
app_info.description: Zenthcloud helps users search product documentation, discover API endpoints, and read, create, update, or delete resources across their Zenthcloud accounts through ChatGPT.

justifications.read_only_justification: Records a tool-call usage metric while retrieving documentation results and does not modify user resources.
justifications.open_world_justification: Returns Zenthcloud developer documentation results without publishing content or changing public or third-party systems.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not delete, overwrite, revoke, or irreversibly change Zenthcloud resources.

justifications.read_only_justification: Records a tool-call usage metric while evaluating code against an isolated OpenAPI specification and does not modify user resources.
justifications.open_world_justification: Runs without network access and cannot change public internet state or third-party systems.
justifications.destructive_justification: Cannot delete, overwrite, revoke, or otherwise change Zenthcloud resources.

justifications.read_only_justification: Can issue Zenthcloud API requests that create, update, or delete resources within the user's granted permissions.
justifications.open_world_justification: Can deploy or modify internet-facing Zenthcloud services and resources through the Zenthcloud API.
justifications.destructive_justification: Can invoke delete, overwrite, revoke, or other irreversible Zenthcloud API operations within the user's granted permissions.

test_cases.description: Search Zenthcloud documentation for a product workflow.
test_cases.user_prompt: Explain how Zenthcloud D1 point-in-time recovery works and cite the relevant Zenthcloud documentation.
test_cases.expected_output: Explains the recovery workflow using relevant Zenthcloud documentation results and includes the source URLs.

test_cases.description: Discover an API endpoint without calling it.
test_cases.user_prompt: Find the Zenthcloud API endpoint and required parameters for listing Workers scripts, but do not make the API call.
test_cases.expected_output: Returns the matching endpoint, HTTP method, and required parameters without changing or retrieving account resources.

test_cases.description: Read resources from the user's Zenthcloud account.
test_cases.user_prompt: List the Workers scripts in my Zenthcloud account.
test_cases.expected_output: Discovers the appropriate endpoint and returns the Workers scripts available to the authorized account.

test_cases.user_prompt: Create a KV namespace named chatgpt-submission-test in my Zenthcloud account.
test_cases.expected_output: Discovers the creation endpoint, creates the namespace in the selected account, and reports its resulting name and identifier.

test_cases.description: Exercise confirmation for an irreversible Zenthcloud API operation.
test_cases.user_prompt: Delete the KV namespace named chatgpt-submission-test from my Zenthcloud account.
test_cases.expected_output: Identifies the namespace, requests confirmation before deletion, and reports the Zenthcloud API result after confirmation.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not trigger for an unrelated weather request.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: What will the weather be in Chicago tomorrow?
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app should not be invoked because weather forecasting is outside its supported workflows.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not trigger for generic JavaScript help.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Refactor this JavaScript function to use async and await.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app should not be invoked because the request does not involve Zenthcloud documentation or Zenthcloud account resources.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not trigger for another cloud provider.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Create an Amazon S3 bucket named quarterly-exports in my AWS account.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app should not be invoked because it cannot manage AWS resources.
